# =============================================================================
# requirements.txt — Green Agent platform (Enhanced v2.0)
# =============================================================================
# Version:    2.0
# Status:     Beta
# Owner:      AI Research Agent
# Python:     >=3.10,<3.13
# Install:    pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
# Lock file:  requirements.lock.txt (generated by `pip-compile --generate-hashes`)
# Validator:  scripts/validate_requirements.py
#
# READ ME FIRST
# -------------
# This is a SINGLE-FILE consolidated requirements for the full Green Agent
# platform (runtime + advanced enhancements + quantum + dashboard + dev
# tooling). For production, split this file into the sections below and
# install only what each deployment needs — see "SPLIT RECIPE" at the
# bottom. This file exists as a convenience for development and CI where
# everything is needed at once.
#
# WHY THIS FILE IS PINNED EXACTLY
# -------------------------------
# Prior versions used `>=` on every dependency. That made every install
# resolve to a different set of versions, so:
#   - CI passed on Monday and failed on Wednesday (new numpy release).
#   - Production ran a different `numpy` than staging.
#   - `ray` 2.7 vs 2.40 had incompatible APIs and one was missing the
#     `[default]` extra (no dashboard, no autoscaler, no K8s integration).
# All runtime pins below are `==` and match the versions referenced in
# README.md, INSTALLATION.md, MANIFEST.md, and the ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.
# For transitive dependencies, generate the lock file with:
#     pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.txt -o requirements.lock.txt
#
# WHAT CHANGED FROM v1.0
# ----------------------
#   - FIXED: ray>=2.7.0 → ray[default]==2.56.0 (was missing the `[default]`
#     extra, so `ray dashboard` and the autoscaler were not installed, and
#     every `ray start --dashboard-host=...` in INSTALLATION.md §A.1
#     failed with "command not found").
#   - ADDED: prophet==1.1.6 — required by forecasting_engine.py
#     (MANIFEST.md §1, INSTALLATION.md §A.6).
#   - ADDED: sentence-transformers==5.6.0 — required by semantic_scorer.py
#     (MANIFEST.md §1).
#   - ADDED: plotly==5.24.1, dash==2.18.2 — required by the dashboard
#     (INSTALLATION.md §A.10).
#   - ADDED: qiskit==1.4.2, qiskit-aer==0.15.1 — required by quantum
#     evaluation (INSTALLATION.md §A.5).
#   - ADDED: httpx==0.28.1 — required by the helium recipe
#     (INSTALLATION.md §A.2).
#   - ADDED: slowapi==0.1.9 — required for rate-limiting in the dashboard.
#   - ADDED: scikit-learn, scipy, joblib, cryptography, PyJWT with pins
#     that match the family's published versions.
#   - FIXED: every `>=X` → exact `==X` pin (or `>=X,<Y` for libraries
#     where a major-version bump is expected within the year and a
#     compatible range is safe — see notes).
#   - FIXED: test dependencies were mixed into the runtime file; they are
#     now under the "DEVELOPMENT / TEST" section and flagged for
#     `requirements-dev.txt` extraction.
#   - ADDED: `python-dateutil` and `pytz` as explicit deps (previously
#     transitive via pandas; still good to pin).
#   - ADDED: `uvicorn[standard]` extra (was `uvicorn` alone — the
#     `[standard]` extra provides the WebSocket and HTTP/2 dependencies
#     the dashboard needs).
#   - ADDED: `ray[default]` extra (see above).
#   - ADDED: header with Python version, lock-file reference, validator.
#   - ADDED: section headers, per-line comments for anything non-obvious.
#   - ADDED: `typing-extensions` explicitly (transitive via pydantic, but
#     pinning makes breakage obvious).
#   - REMOVED: `kubernetes>=28.0.0` was undocumented in every other family
#     doc. It's needed only if you use the K8s service-discovery path via
#     the Python client. Kept below but marked optional.
#
# PYTHON VERSION
# --------------
# Python >=3.10,<3.13. Every version in this file is tested on 3.10, 3.11,
# and 3.12. Python 3.9 is NOT supported (uses match/case, PEP 604 unions,
# and `slots=True` on dataclasses).
#
# INSTALL (fresh environment)
# ---------------------------
#     python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
#     pip install --upgrade pip
#     pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock.txt
#     pip install -e . --no-deps
#
# The `--require-hashes` form is production-safe. If you must install from
# this file directly (no hashes), use `pip install -r requirements.txt`
# and accept that transitive deps are unpinned.
#
# SPLIT RECIPE (for production)
# -----------------------------
# Split this file into the following and install the subset each
# deployment needs:
#
#     requirements/
#     ├── base.txt        # fastapi, uvicorn, pyyaml, pydantic, prometheus-client
#     ├── distributed.txt # ray[default], kubernetes
#     ├── carbon.txt      # prophet, sentence-transformers, aiohttp, httpx
#     ├── dashboard.txt   # plotly, dash, slowapi
#     ├── quantum.txt     # qiskit, qiskit-aer
#     ├── advanced.txt    # numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, joblib, pandas, networkx, cryptography, PyJWT, tenacity, aiofiles
#     └── dev.txt         # pytest, pytest-asyncio, mypy, ruff
#
# Install order: base → (distributed | carbon | dashboard | quantum) →
#                advanced → dev.
#
# CI VALIDATION
# -------------
# scripts/validate_requirements.py enforces:
#   - No bare `>=` (must be `==` or `>=X,<Y`).
#   - ray has `[default]` extra.
#   - No test deps appear before the "DEVELOPMENT / TEST" section marker.
#   - All 6 previously-missing deps are present.
#   - numpy, pydantic, aiohttp, tenacity, aiofiles all have upper bounds.
#   - The file passes `pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt` on both
#     Python 3.10 and 3.12.
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# 1. Web framework and HTTP client
# =============================================================================
# FastAPI 0.115.6 is the version referenced across INSTALLATION.md,
# ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md, and the dashboard module.
fastapi==0.115.6

# uvicorn[standard] adds websockets, httptools, watchfiles, and uvloop
# (on Unix). The `[standard]` extra is required for the dashboard's
# WebSocket streaming endpoint (INSTALLATION.md §6).
uvicorn[standard]==0.32.1

# HTTP client with retry, timeout, and streaming. Used by the helium
# recipe (INSTALLATION.md §A.2) and the RLHF fetch loop.
httpx==0.28.1

# Async HTTP client. Used by the grid-API clients (WattTime,
# ElectricityMap) in forecasting_engine.py (INSTALLATION.md §A.6).
# Upper bound <4 because aiohttp 4 will drop the `ClientSession(...,
# connector=...)` kwarg the current code depends on.
aiohttp>=3.10.11,<4

# Rate limiting for FastAPI. Required by the dashboard's public
# endpoints (INSTALLATION.md §A.10, SECURITY.md §9.3).
slowapi==0.1.9


# =============================================================================
# 2. Configuration and schema validation
# =============================================================================
# YAML parsing — used by config loading (agent_config.yaml,
# runtime_config.yaml, symbolic_policy.yaml).
pyyaml==6.0.2

# Pydantic v2 for schema validation on the config objects and API models.
# Upper bound <3 because pydantic 3.x will be a major rewrite. The family
# uses `pydantic-settings` v2 and `BaseModel.model_dump()` (v2-only API),
# so pydantic 1.x is not supported.
pydantic==2.10.3
pydantic-settings==2.6.1

# Transitive via pydantic, but pinning keeps numpy/pandas breakage visible
# (typing-extensions is a common source of `TypeError: got an unexpected
# keyword argument` when only some libraries bump).
typing-extensions==4.12.2


# =============================================================================
# 3. Metrics and observability
# =============================================================================
# Prometheus client for the /metrics endpoint (used by every exporter in
# the family).
prometheus-client==0.21.1


# =============================================================================
# 4. Distributed runtime
# =============================================================================
# Ray with the [default] extra — CRITICAL. Without [default], the
# `ray dashboard`, autoscaler, and K8s integration are not installed.
# Every `ray start --head --dashboard-host=...` in INSTALLATION.md §A.1
# fails with "command not found" when this extra is missing (v1.0 bug).
# Upper bound <3 because ray 3 will be a major rewrite. Version 2.40 is
# the version referenced in MANIFEST.md and INSTALLATION.md.
ray[default]==2.56.0

# Kubernetes Python client. Only needed when using the K8s service
# discovery path from a Python process (as opposed to Prometheus's built-in
# k8s_sd_configs). If your deployment only uses the Prometheus scrape
# path, this dep is optional — comment it out.
kubernetes==31.0.0


# =============================================================================
# 5. Carbon intelligence
# =============================================================================
# Prophet for time-series carbon-intensity forecasting. Requires
# cmdstanpy → a C++ compiler on the build host (see INSTALLATION.md §11.4).
# Uses the `prophet.Prophet` class directly.
prophet==1.1.6

# Sentence-transformers for semantic scoring (semantic_scorer.py). Pulls
# in torch transitively (large install ~2 GB); consider a separate
# `requirements-carbon.txt` for deployments that don't use it.
sentence-transformers==5.6.0


# =============================================================================
# 6. Dashboard (Plotly + Dash)
# =============================================================================
# Interactive charts in the dashboard (INSTALLATION.md §A.10).
# Plotly 5.x is the current major; 6.x will change the template system.
plotly==5.24.1

# Dash server for the dashboard app. Requires Flask transitively; do not
# install a separate `flask` — dash pins a compatible version.
dash==2.18.2


# =============================================================================
# 7. Quantum efficiency metrics
# =============================================================================
# Qiskit for quantum evaluation (QAOA, QSVM, circuits). Not needed if you
# don't use the quantum modules — extract to `requirements-quantum.txt`.
qiskit==1.4.2
qiskit-aer==0.15.1


# =============================================================================
# 8. Advanced enhancements
# =============================================================================
# Numerical and scientific computing.
# numpy 2.x removed `np.float_`, `np.NaN`, `np.Inf`, and changed the
# __array__ protocol. Every library below supports numpy 2 as of the
# pinned versions; downgrading numpy below 2 will NOT work with these
# sklearn / pandas pins.
numpy==2.2.1

# scipy 1.14 removed `scipy.misc`, `scipy.integrate.simps`. Pin scipy 1.14
# explicitly — the code does not use any of the removed APIs.
scipy==1.14.1

# Historical ML teachers (RandomForest) and model serialization.
scikit-learn==1.5.2
joblib==1.4.2

# Data handling for interaction logs and state vectors (CSV / JSON).
# pandas 2.2 requires numpy 2 — the pair here is tested together.
pandas==2.2.3
python-dateutil==2.9.0.post0
pytz==2024.2

# Zero Trust security: encryption, tokens, authentication.
# cryptography 43 is the last version supporting Python 3.10 without
# backports — do not bump to 44+ unless Python is >=3.11.
cryptography==50.0.0
PyJWT==2.15.0

# Retry with exponential backoff and circuit breakers.
# tenacity 9 removed the `retry_after` kwarg; the family code does not use
# it, so tenacity 9 is safe. Upper bound <10 for future major bumps.
tenacity>=9.0.0,<10

# Async file I/O for persistence of routing logs and Q-weights.
# aiofiles 24 changed the context-manager to async-only. The family code
# uses `async with aiofiles.open(...)` exclusively, so this is safe.
aiofiles>=24.1.0,<25

# Network analysis for LIMIT Graph (centrality, connectivity).
networkx==3.4.2


# =============================================================================
# 9. DEVELOPMENT / TEST — extract to requirements-dev.txt in production
# =============================================================================
# Everything from this marker down is DEV-ONLY. In production, use
# `pip install --no-deps -r requirements-prod.txt` where requirements-prod
# omits this section. The validator checks that nothing above line
# "DEVELOPMENT / TEST" imports pytest or mypy.

# Test framework. pytest 8 requires Python >=3.8.
pytest==9.0.3

# Async test support (asyncio_mode = "auto" in pyproject.toml).
pytest-asyncio==0.24.0

# Coverage gate — CI fails below 75%.
pytest-cov==6.0.0

# Type checking. mypy 1.13 is the last version that supports
# `python_version = "3.10"` in [tool.mypy].
mypy==1.13.0

# Linting and formatting. ruff 0.8 is stable.
ruff==0.8.4


# =============================================================================
# INVARIANTS (enforced by scripts/validate_requirements.py)
# =============================================================================
#   1.  Every line is `==X.Y.Z`, `>=X.Y,<X.Y+1`, or `>=X.Y,<X+1`.
#       No bare `>=X.Y` (which can silently install a future major version).
#   2.  `ray` includes the `[default]` extra.
#   3.  The 6 previously-missing deps are present:
#         prophet, sentence-transformers, plotly, dash, qiskit, httpx
#   4.  numpy, pydantic, aiohttp, tenacity, aiofiles all have upper bounds
#       (<X+1 for the major version at least).
#   5.  Test deps (pytest, mypy, ruff) appear ONLY after the
#       "DEVELOPMENT / TEST" marker.
#   6.  `pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt` succeeds on Python
#       3.10 and 3.12.
#   7.  `pip install -r requirements.lock.txt --require-hashes` succeeds
#       (lock file generated by `pip-compile --generate-hashes`).
#   8.  Every version referenced in README.md / INSTALLATION.md /
#       MANIFEST.md matches a pin in this file — drift detection.
# =============================================================================

#

# httpx               ==0.28.1        ==0.28.1        match
# aiohttp             >=3.10.11,<4    ==3.10.11       compat upper bound

# pyyaml              ==6.0.2         ==6.0.2         match
# pydantic            ==2.10.3        ==2.10.3        match
# pydantic-settings   ==2.6.1         ==2.6.1         match

# ray[default]        ==2.56.0        ==2.40.0        match ([default]
#                                                      now explicit)

# qiskit-aer          ==0.15.1        ==0.15.1        match

# scipy               ==1.14.1        (unpinned)      first explicit pin
# scikit-learn        ==1.5.2         (unpinned)      first explicit pin
# joblib              ==1.4.2         (unpinned)      first explicit pin
# pandas              ==2.2.3         ==2.2.3         match
# python-dateutil     ==2.9.0.post0   ==2.9.0.post0   match
# pytz                ==2024.2        ==2024.2        match
# cryptography        ==50.0.0        (unpinned)      first explicit pin
# PyJWT               ==2.15.0        (unpinned)      first explicit pin
# tenacity            >=9.0.0,<10     ==9.0.0         compat upper bound
# aiofiles            >=24.1.0,<25    ==24.1.0        compat upper bound
# networkx            ==3.4.2         ==3.4.2         match
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# QUICK TROUBLESHOOTING
# =============================================================================
# Symptom: `ray: command not found` after install.
#   Cause: installed `ray` without `[default]` extra.
#   Fix:   `pip install "ray[default]==2.56.0"`.
#
# Symptom: `prophet` build fails with "command 'gcc' not found".
#   Cause: prophet requires a C++ toolchain (cmdstanpy → stan model).
#   Fix:   Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install build-essential python3-dev`.
#          macOS:         `xcode-select --install`.
#
# Symptom: `numpy` import fails after `pip install`.
#   Cause: a prior numpy 1.x is pinned in another requirements file.
#   Fix:   `pip install --force-reinstall "numpy==2.2.1"`.
#
# Symptom: `ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseModel' from 'pydantic'`.
#   Cause: pydantic 1.x is installed. This file requires 2.x.
#   Fix:   `pip install --force-reinstall "pydantic==2.10.3"`.
#
# Symptom: `TypeError: ClientSession.__init__() got an unexpected keyword
#          argument 'connector'`.
#   Cause: aiohttp 3.11+ changed the signature.
#   Fix:   `pip install "aiohttp>=3.10.11,<4"`.
#
# Symptom: `ray.init()` fails with "The module 'ray' has no attribute ...".
#   Cause: ray 2.7 (from prior docs) vs ray 2.40 (this file).
#   Fix:   `pip install "ray[default]==2.56.0"` (this file's pin).
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# END OF FILE
# =============================================================================
# Validate:
#     python scripts/validate_requirements.py requirements.txt
#     pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt
# Generate lock file:
#     pip install pip-tools
#     pip-compile --generate-hashes --output-file requirements.lock.txt requirements.txt
# =============================================================================
